spec.title: Install vibe
spec.p: vibe is one program with no runtime to install. On Windows you download an archive and unpack it; on any platform with a Rust toolchain you build it from the source. When it is done, one command prints the version.
spec.prompt: Install vibe on this machine: on Windows from the latest release archive at github.com/vibevm/vibevm, otherwise by building the source checkout with its first-run script. Then open a new shell and confirm that `vibe --version` prints a version. network access to github.com; on a platform other than Windows, git and a Rust toolchain `vibe --version` prints `vibe 1.0.0` in a new terminal, and `vibe self doctor` reports no problems vibe --version vibe self doctor

what-happens.title: What happens
what-happens.p: On Windows the agent downloads the release archive, unpacks it, and runs its installer script. The script imports the binary into vibe's own managed folder under `~/.vibe/opt`, marks it active, and adds one folder of small launcher scripts to your user `PATH`. Everywhere else the agent clones the source repository and runs its first-run script, which builds the program and installs it through the same manager. Either way, the result is the same layout: versions under `~/.vibe/opt/vibevm/`, launchers in `~/.vibe/opt/bin/`, and a pointer that says which version is current.

windows.title: On Windows
windows.p: 1. Download `vibe-<version>-windows-x86_64.zip` from the releases page of `github.com/vibevm/vibevm`.
2. Unpack the archive into a folder of your choice.
3. In that folder run the installer:
4. Open a new terminal, so that the changed `PATH` is read.
The archive also contains `SHA256SUMS.txt`. Compare the digest of `vibe.exe` with the line in that file before you run the installer. The installer does the same check.

from-source.title: From the source, on any platform
from-source.p: 1. Install git and a Rust toolchain. OpenSSL is not needed.
2. Clone the repository: `git clone https://github.com/vibevm/vibevm.git` and enter the folder.

3. Run the first-run script: `bash tools/first-run.sh` on Linux and macOS, `.\tools\first-run.ps1` on Windows. It builds the program, installs it into the managed [store](../glossary/index.xml#store) and sets up the launchers.
4. Open a new terminal and run `vibe --version`, then `vibe self doctor`.
Later, `vibe self install latest` rebuilds from the tip of the main branch. `vibe self ls` lists the versions on the machine, and `vibe self rollback` returns to the previous one.

where-things-go.title: Where things go
where-things-go.p: vibe keeps everything it owns under one folder in your home directory, `~/.vibe/`: the installed versions and their launchers under `opt/`, the machine store of fetched packages under `cache/`, [registry](../glossary/index.xml#registry) clones under `registries/`, and your settings files. Nothing is written anywhere else, and the whole folder can be moved by setting the environment variable `VIBE_SETTINGS`.
The installer never overwrites a running binary and never edits your `PATH` twice: it adds one entry, guarded by a marker, and leaves the rest alone.

edge-cases.title: Edge cases and rules
edge-cases.p: If `vibe --version` prints nothing in the terminal where you ran the installer, open a new one: the `PATH` change applies to new shells only.
A ready-built binary from anywhere can join the managed store without a toolchain: `vibe self import ./vibe.exe --tag 1.0.0 --use`.
Building an arbitrary git ref is running arbitrary code, as with any build from source. Build from the repository and the branches you trust.
